pipeline.name: Neural source
pipeline.what_happens: Neurons in the hand-knob region of motor cortex (precentral gyrus) fire action potentials when the participant attempts/imagines hand and arm movement.

facts.fact: Implant target located pre-op with fMRI of attempted hand/arm movement; target on precentral gyrus
Link records from the hand-knob region of motor cortex
Signals from both hands are decodable despite single-hemisphere implant

pipeline.name: Electrodes / threads (sensing)
pipeline.what_happens: Flexible polymer threads carrying electrode sites sit near neurons and pick up extracellular voltage (µV-scale).

facts.fact: N1: 1,024 electrodes across 64 flexible threads
Planned increase from ~1,000 to ~3,000 electrodes; exploring thread-retention features and through-dura insertion
2019 platform: 32 electrodes/thread, threads 5–50 µm wide, 4–6 µm thick, polyimide with gold traces; up to 3,072 electrodes on 96 threads
Electrode impedance @1 kHz: PEDOT:PSS ~37 kΩ, IrOx ~56 kΩ (2019)
R1 robot inserts threads; 2019 robot: up to 6 threads (192 electrodes)/min, 87.1% insertion success

pipeline.name: Analog front end + digitisation (on-implant ASIC)
pipeline.what_happens: Each channel is amplified, band-pass filtered and digitised by custom low-power chips.

facts.fact: 2019 ASIC: 256 channels/ASIC, gain 42.9–59.4 dB, bandwidth 3 Hz–27 kHz, input-referred noise 5.9 µVrms, 10-bit ADC @ 19.3 kHz, 5.2 µW/channel, ~6 mW/ASIC
N1: 1,024 electrodes @ ~20 kHz, 10-bit resolution → ~200 Mbps raw
Raw rate check: 1024 × 20,000 × 10 bit = 204.8 Mbps

pipeline.name: On-implant processing / compression
pipeline.what_happens: Raw broadband data is far too large for the radio, so the implant reduces it (spike detection / feature extraction / compression) before transmission.

facts.fact: Wireless link carries only ~1 Mbps, so >200× reduction is required; real-time, <1 ms latency, <10 mW power budget
Patent: filter signal, fit to a model, compare characteristic values to thresholds to declare a spike; fixed-point arithmetic; spikes + timestamps packetised for wireless transmission
Best community lossless ratio ~4.4×, implying the production path is lossy (spike events / features), not raw waveform
Custom low-power chips process neural signals before wireless transmission
After thread retraction (2024) Neuralink 'modified the recording algorithm to be more sensitive to neural population signals'
Decoder input is spiking events per channel (participant 1 alone: 9,000+ hours ≈ 22.4 billion spikes)

pipeline.name: Wireless link + power
pipeline.what_happens: Processed neural data is radioed through the scalp to an external device; battery recharged inductively.

facts.fact: Data transmitted wirelessly to the Neuralink Application on a computer/phone; battery inductively recharged by N1 Charger; no physical connectors
2019 research system used wired USB-C and 10 GbE UDP multicast base station (pre-wireless)
Radio commonly described as Bluetooth/BLE-class

pipeline.name: Decoding (Neuralink Application, ML)
pipeline.what_happens: ML models convert spike streams into intended actions (cursor velocity, click type, finger/key, robot-arm DOF).

facts.fact: Decoders are user-specific and trained via calibration tasks; users averaged 55 min/week of calibration (old system ~10 min/day)
2026 encoder: Mamba (state-space) backbone; spikes treated as tokens with per-channel learned embeddings (POYO-style); Perceiver input layer; fully causal
Self-supervised objective: spatially masked auto-Poisson regression — feed half the channels, predict the other half
Pretrained on >50,000 h unlabeled free-use neural data; 30 s labeled embeddings ≈ 3.5 min raw-spike calibration
Decoders now last >1 week; some >3 weeks; one usable 20 months after calibration
Cross-participant transfer: P9-trained model worked for P2 with 99% weights frozen, beating P2's own decoder
Exploring decoding of cursor/target position and 'cursor teleportation' (>10 BPS in initial tests)

pipeline.name: Post-processing / UI
pipeline.what_happens: Decoded intents are smoothed, gated and mapped to OS input events and app modes.

facts.fact: Previously used smoothing, low-velocity suppression and click post-processing (added delay); pretrained decoders made several of these unnecessary
Mode switcher UI maps intended movements to left/right/middle click, zoom, scroll, pan, drag
Cursor + multi-click control of laptop/phone: chess, Civilization VI, Mario Kart, Counter-Strike, CAD (Fusion 360), Illustrator
Ten-finger 'keyboard for the mind' typing up to 40 WPM
CONVOY: assistive robotic arm control (feeding, gesturing); 7+ DOF in simulation
VOICE trial targets speech at ~140 WPM from speech-production cortex
Blindsight (vision) received FDA Breakthrough Device Designation 2024-09-17

program_stats.stat: 3 participants; >670 implant-days; >4,900 h use; 6.5 h/day independent use
21 participants enrolled worldwide; higher signal quality in 18 of 20 post-mitigation participants; zero serious device-related adverse events
>50,000 h unlabeled neural data streamed by participants

latest_model.name: Participant-specific self-supervised neural encoder + task decoder heads
architecture: spike-as-token input with per-channel learned embeddings (POYO-style)
Mamba state-space backbone (causal, constant low-latency inference)
small decoder heads: cursor velocity, click probabilities, robot-arm 7+ DOF; linear position probes for 'cursor teleportation'
latest_model.pretraining: spatially masked auto-Poisson regression on >50,000 h unlabeled free-use recordings (P1 alone >9,000 h / 22.4B spikes)

results.calibration: 10 min/day -> as low as 10 min/week; 30 s embeddings ~= 3.5 min raw spikes
results.longevity: >1 week typical, >3 weeks some, usable at 20 months in one case

latest_model.limits: all live results use single-participant pretraining; multi-participant pooled models not yet better online; cross-participant transfer shown (P9->P2, 99% weights frozen)

latest_data.public_release: None. Neuralink has not released neural data or model weights. Its only open-source data tool is the datarepo catalog library (2025-06-22), explicitly 'not a release of any Neuralink data'. The Hugging Face 'neuralink' account (cartpole, xlm-roberta) appears unrelated to the company.

latest_hardware_surgery.item: First transdural (through-dura) insertion, UHN Toronto; Lee Marten (ALS) first such patient
Next-gen ~3,000-electrode implant planned; no confirmed human deployment found
Reported Samsung order for next-gen implant processor; PCTFE enclosure patent published

latest_outputs.item: VOICE trial video: participant produced 'I love you' as synthesized speech in pre-illness voice from silent/imagined speech; phoneme decoding + personalised TTS; delay of several seconds; no accuracy/latency figures published
First thought-to-speech demo (Kenneth Shock, ALS, implanted Jan 2026)
VOICE (NCT07224256) at UT Southwestern; output verbal thought as text or speech; target ~140 WPM
Blindsight: no confirmed first human implant found
